newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down after two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down after two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended down on Wednesday compared to its previous New York close after two-way trade from Japan and European sales, gold traders said.
Bullion ended at US$342.30/80 an ounce on Wednesday against New York's US$342.70/343.20 close on Tuesday.
"There was two-way trade from Japan, still following currency movements," said one bullion dealer.
Firmer platinum boosted gold buying, dealers said.
"Gold pushed $343.50 per ounce, when platinum touched a high and the dollar retreated, so there was a bit of gold buying," another source noted.
When Europe opened, gold came under selling pressure, with dealers in Hong Kong noting the sales as dollar-related arbitraging.
There was still physical demand in the market, but it was average, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$1 lower at HK$3,164 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -5.00
